statements.text: Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. is undertaking structural reforms aimed at improving the profitability of its U.S. operations in response to cost increases resulting from U.S. tariffs and changes in the market environment
Yamaha already employs over 2,300 Georgians across various facilities, including its 1.3-million-square-foot factory in Newman
Yamaha Motor Corporation is moving its U.S. headquarters to Georgia after half a century in California to increase profitability amid higher costs from tariffs.

Yamaha Motor U.S. intends to sell all fixed assets owned by the company in Cypress, California, including land, offices and warehouses. The Japanese company expects the move to help combat tariffs by improving efficiency and profitability in the U.S. market.
The Japanese manufacturer, best known for its motorcycles and ATVs, is selling its over-25-acre site in California as part of the transition, including the land, offices, and warehouses.

Sina Golara added that Yamaha Motor Corp. is an international company, so part of its supply chain originates from outside the U.S. They make some parts, then move them to plants here for final manufacturing and sale.
